title: Penn World Table 10.01: Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore and the United States, 1950-2019
source: Penn World Table version 10.01, Groningen Growth and Development Centre, University of Groningen (DataverseNL, doi:10.34894/QT5BCC, released 2023-01-26)
series: countrycode, country, year; in the words of the sheet Legend: rgdpna ('Real GDP at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)'), rnna ('Capital stock at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)'), emp ('Number of persons engaged (in millions)'), avh ('Average annual hours worked by persons engaged'), hc ('Human capital index, based on years of schooling and returns to education; see Human capital in PWT9.'), labsh ('Share of labour compensation in GDP at current national prices'), rgdpe ('Expenditure-side real GDP at chained PPPs (in mil. 2017US$)'), pop ('Population (in millions)'), csh_i ('Share of gross capital formation at current PPPs'), i_outlier and i_xr (the workbook's own flags)
license: CC BY 4.0: the record of the dataset on DataverseNL (doi:10.34894/QT5BCC) gives the licence as 'CC-BY-4.0' (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0), as recorded for Chapter 40 in data/snapshots/pwt1001_usa.json. Its description asks: 'When using these data (for whatever purpose), please make the following reference: Feenstra, Robert C., Robert Inklaar and Marcel P. Timmer (2015), "The Next Generation of the Penn World Table" American Economic Review, 105(10), 3150-3182, DOI: 10.1257/aer.20130954, available for download at www.ggdc.net/pwt'. The book cites Feenstra, Inklaar and Timmer (2015) with the database (bibitem pwt1001) in the table and the figures, and says there that the growth accounting is its own calculation.
citation: Feenstra, Robert C., Robert Inklaar and Marcel P. Timmer (2015), "The Next Generation of the Penn World Table", American Economic Review 105(10): 3150-3182 (bibitem pwt1001 of Chapter 40)
notes: Read from the workbook pwt1001.xlsx, sheet Data, downloaded from https://dataverse.nl/api/access/datafile/354095 (SHA-256 bf2b66c5fd8b465870eeab8bbfa3a57e73253a3236a933286259efbbb5fb67a2), the copy of Chapter 40. Every year 1950-2019 of the six economies, empty where the workbook has no figure (Korea before 1953, Taiwan in 1950, Hong Kong and Singapore before 1960). The figures are written as the workbook stores them (Python's repr of the float). The workbook's own flags: i_outlier is 'Regular' in every year with data (no year of these six economies is marked 'Outlier'); i_xr is empty in the years without data and 'Market-based' otherwise. The labour share labsh is the same number for long runs of years at the start: Japan 1950-1980, Korea 1953-1970, Hong Kong and Singapore 1960-1980, Taiwan 1951-2000 (checks/check_ch42.py finds the runs); the book uses the figures as they stand and says so. checks/check_ch42.py computes the growth accounting of eq:eastasia-accounting (logarithmic growth rates between the end years, the capital share one minus the mean labsh of the years of the period), the levels of rgdpe/pop relative to the United States for fig:eastasia_levels, and the comparisons with Young (1994) and Collins and Bosworth (1996).
